Rules To Be Followed When Creating Mout Poster
RULES TO BE FOLLOWED WHEN CREATING MOUT POSTER
The objective of this brand guide is to provide clear
creating posters, designs, and related materials for Murang’a
University Team. It ensures that all communication reflects
the university’s identity in a professional, cohesive, and
recognizable way. The guidelines promote uniformity in
colors, typography, imagery, and layout, helping to
Colors play a key role in maintaining a strong and consistent brand identity.
All posters, designs, and communication materials should use the official
Murang’a University brand colors to ensure uniformity and recognition.
The primary colors should always be dominant, while secondary colors
may be applied sparingly to support the design without overpowering the
main palette. Designers must avoid using random or off-brand shades to keep
the visual identity clean, professional, and easily recognizable.
Our primary brand color is Green
It represents growth, freshness, and stability. This
color should be dominant in all designs—used for titles, highlights, and key elements.
Always keep it consistent and avoid altering its shade or tone.
Our secondary brand color is Maroon
This maroon complements the primary green, adding balance, strength, and a sense
of tradition. It should be used sparingly—mainly for accents, headings,
or supportive design elements—without overpowering the
Black provides strength, contrast, and professionalism.
It should be used mainly for text, outlines, and elements
where clarity and emphasis are required.
White represents purity, simplicity, and space. It serves as the background
color in most designs, ensuring readability and a clean, modern look.
Together, black and white support the primary and secondary colors,
creating balance and maintaining visual consistency.
Poppins – Modern, clean, and highly readable. Ideal for body text,
Futura – Geometric and professional. Best for titles, emphasis, and formal print materials.
These two fonts form the core of the brand identity and should
be used consistently across all official designs.
Fonts majorly used in Theme words, letters , dates etc includes; but In themes , no any other font
is used except poppins and futura;
Script fonts may be used creatively for accents, quotes, or decorative elements.
They are not limited but should complement the primary fonts without
Avoid overusing script fonts to maintain a professional and clean look.
